rawItems.title: Wild Wood Festival returns for 11th edition with 2manydjs and Crazy P on line-up
rawItems.content: An independent electronic music festival is returning for its eleventh edition, promising three days and nights of discovery in a woodland setting. Wild Wood Festival, held in South Cambridgeshire, will run from June 18 to 21, 2027 and will feature a mix of international artists, underground favourites and emerging talent. This year’s line-up includes 2manydjs, Crazy P (DJ), Colleen 'Cosmo' Murphy, Gerd Janson, David Holmes, Eris Drew B2B Octo Octa, Roman Flügel, Guy Williams, and Midland. Party partners and stage takeovers will include Phonica Records, The Golden Lion, Tryouts, Margate Arts Club, Me Me Me, and Club Cowgirl. Vicky Fenton, founder of the festival, said: "There’s something about Wild Wood that’s hard to put into words. "Wild Wood is a world of its own, a place where you can discover your next favourite artist and make memories with people who quickly feel like old friends. "It’s the unexpected discoveries, the incredible energy, the music you didn’t know you needed to hear and the feeling of being somewhere completely removed from everyday life. "We want people to arrive with an open mind and leave with stories they’ll be talking about for months." The festival will showcase house, techno, disco and Balearic sounds across multiple woodland stages, including its iconic vortex-shaped main stage, redesigned Lost Stage and hidden dance floors. rawItems.title: Jonathan Agnew headlines sold-out St Neots fundraiser for local charities
rawItems.content:
A sold-out audience gathered at St Neots Golf Club to hear cricket commentator Jonathan Agnew share stories from the world of Test cricket at a Rotary Club fundraiser. Mr Agnew, an ex England cricketer and now lead commentator on BBC Radio’s 5 Live Test Match Special, headlined the latest Sportsman’s Lunch hosted by the Rotary Club of St Neots St Marys on Friday, November 6. He entertained guests with a mixture of video clips and anecdotes from his many years in the commentary box. Jonathan Agnew (middle) pictured with members of the Rotary club. (Image: Jonathan Agnew sharing cricket stories.) This was the 38th event in a series that began in 1990 and has since raised well over £250,000. In the Rotary year ending 30th June 2026 the club distributed just over £22,000 to local and international charities and good causes approximately 80% staying in the local area. Donations ranged from £100 to £4000 and so far in the current Rotary year around £13,000 has already been raised. Read more Huntingdon venue seeks permission to extend weekend opening activities

rawItems.title: Ramsey Cricket Club pays tribute to much-loved member after more than 40 years
rawItems.content: A Huntingdonshire cricket club has paid tribute to a "much-loved" member who dedicated more than 40 years to the game. Richard 'Nobby' Clarke, described as a lifetime member of Ramsey Cricket Club (RCC), died earlier this week. Richard 'Nobby' Clarke (Image: Ramsey Cricket Club Facebook) In a post on the club's Facebook page, a spokesman for RCC said: "It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Richard 'Nobby' Clarke, who passed away on Monday morning. "Nobby was a lifetime member of RCC and a much-loved part of our club community. "Rest in peace, Nobby. "Thank you for everything you gave to RCC." The Hunts Post has set up a book of condolence for people to share their memories of Richard 'Nobby' Clarke, who was described as a lifetime member of Ramsey Cricket Club.
